title: Phantom Blade Zero Walkthrough - Chapter Order and What Locks When
description: Phantom Blade Zero's main story in order: 8 regions, 22 missions, the point of no return at the Mount Soulrend climb, and which optional Tales expire before you get there.

sections.title: How the Campaign Is Structured
sections.content:
Eight semi-open regions in a fixed order, with the Mirage Estate slotted in before the final climb, each with a story thread and a pile of optional content. The game calls its side content Tales; purple Tales are the ones tied to the true ending.

This is not an open world. You cannot wander into Pangzhen from the prologue, and the regions unlock in sequence. What you can do is leave a region early - and that is where runs go wrong, because several Tales stop being completable once the story moves past them.

Fast travel is by bells, one or more per region. Bells do not work inside the Phantom Illusionist Ruins, which is why the Four Guardians' Mirror realm is a one-way trip until you clear it.

Region-by-region layouts, the bell network and per-map completion are on the map guide; the boss-by-boss order is on boss order.

Two caveats. Mission-to-region assignment varies between outlets - Heartless Remnants is put in Village of Lu by one list and in Crimson Forest by another, and Pillars of Kunlun moves between Mandate Encampment and Mount Soulrend depending on who is writing. The order of the missions is consistent across sources; the region labels are not. Treat the sequence as reliable and the borders as approximate.

sections.title: Walkthrough, Chapter by Chapter
sections.content:
This is the walkthrough in the order you actually play it: nine chapters - eight regions plus the Mirage Estate - and 60 encounters, and the three places where leaving early costs you content permanently. Each chapter below gives the story bosses in sequence, the optional fights in it, and what closes it. Fight-by-fight detail lives on the individual boss pages and on boss order; the purpose of this walkthrough is to stop you from walking past something.

Chapter 1: Prologue & Weeping Creek Valley

The walkthrough opens the way the game does: a scripted duel you cannot lose, then a pursuit on the main road. Zuo Shang's opening fight is a tutorial, so use it to learn what a red flash reads like rather than to win fast. The Hunt is not killed here, it comes back later. The valley ends at the Axemaster's Fall, where Peng Meng hands you the Dread Axe, your first Phantom Edge.

Story bosses, in order: Zuo Shang (prologue duel) → The Hunt → Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute → Peng Meng, the Axemaster (斧老大 彭猛).

Optional in this chapter: Hua, Deadly Betrothed (新娘阿花), Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet, The Gold-Masked One (3 of the 7 encounters here are optional).

Do not leave without: Hua, Deadly Betrothed sits in the Flesh Lily Fields and is the most valuable detour in the region. Her Scarlet Wraithblade is scaled for this point; come back at chapter four and the fight is worse for the same reward.

Chapter 2: Crimson Manor & Crimson Forest

Crimson Manor is optional content wrapped around a required trip, which is why people clear it by accident. The forest proper is where the game teaches its elemental vocabulary: Hua Qianxiao's drinking shield at the Pangzhen Bridge Overlook, then Jing Ye's horse and blood-draining sword. Bai Chilian closes the chapter at the Threadbound Great Tree, after the mirror sequence.

Story bosses, in order: Hua Qianxiao, the Sword Fanatic (剑痴 花千笑) → Jing Ye, the Outlaw (亡命徒 荆野) → Bai Chilian, Lady of the Twin Serpents (双蛇夫人 白赤练).

Optional in this chapter: Puppet Scavenger, Acolyte Hansui, Stone Hand Iron Fever (拳痴 铁狂), Jade Dancer and Iron Fiend, Yucong, the Twisted Puppet (No. 34) (5 of the 8 encounters here are optional).

Do not leave without: Acolyte Hansui is reached through a scarecrow and is the easiest fight in the region to walk past. The Gold-Masked One carries over from the valley and keeps returning through the Lóng Pillar trials, so treat each sighting as homework rather than a wall.

Chapter 3: Village of Lu

The densest optional region and the one most often finished too fast. Zhuo Bi guards the approach; the Bi brothers split between the Puppet Testing Grounds route and the village itself. Yuzan needs a drop into the puppet well after Bi Hai, which is the single most missed step in this chapter. Mu Xiaokui closes it with Yu Yao and Tie present.

Story bosses, in order: Zhuo Bi, the Gatekeeper → Master Bi Yuan → Master Bi Hai → Yuzan, the Musician Puppet (三号乐偶师 玉瓒) → Mu Xiaokui, Young Mistress of the Order (沐小葵).

Optional in this chapter: Dusk, the Puppeteer, Acolyte Yanru (2 of the 7 encounters here are optional).

Do not leave without: Dusk, the Puppeteer is gated behind Memory Flowers and will not appear until they are collected. Acolyte Yanru hides behind a terrace bell on the north side of the rice fields.

Chapter 4: Pangzhen

The largest region and the widest missable window, which is a bad combination. The story line runs from the South Gate bridge through the Statue Grounds, the Back Street Archway, the Singing Pond and up from the Three Ships Well before Chang Hong and Flame close it. Flame is the only story boss in the game who gates an optional fight: the Flaming Mane he drops opens the way into Pangzhen Slums.

Story bosses, in order: Blaze, Shadow Warden Captain (鬼差队长 火流星) → Wu Xuan, the Fallen General (堕落将军 武轩) → Gu Wanyue (女妖 骨婉约) → Xie Qiudong, the Divine Healer (神医 谢秋冬) → Chang Hong, the Thunder Spear (长鸿) → Flame, the Lion Dance Grandmaster (舞狮尊主 烈焰).

Optional in this chapter: Cavalrybane (鬼差高手 斩骑), You Loong, Blackwater Crew Leader (游龙), Soulclaimer (勾魂), Zhu Yuan, Acolyte Lei Ting (5 of the 11 encounters here are optional).

Do not leave without: Acolyte Lei Ting is behind that gate, so skipping Flame's drop costs you a fight permanently. You Loong runs through the Green Serpent House and then the water, and is easy to start without finishing in the same visit.

Chapter 5: Mandate Encampment

A shorter chapter that hides one of the game's few formation fights: the Chief Disciple of the Seven-Stars Formation only becomes available once the surrounding disciples are cleared. Push the encampment itself first, then clear outward.

Story bosses, in order: Corpse-Eating Xue → Wan Jun, the Coppermaul → Red, the Mysterious Wraith → Chief Disciple of the Seven-Stars Formation.

Optional in this chapter: Wu Lengshuang, the Soft Sword (柔剑 武林霜), Yubi, the Swordfighter Puppet (No. 21) (2 of the 6 encounters here are optional).

Do not leave without: Wu Lengshuang sits off the Path of the Baishan's Fall, away from the main route. Yubi is in the Training Grounds past the main gate.

Chapter 6: Meigu Lake

Only one story boss, which makes Meigu Lake the region people rush and then regret. Grief-Stricken Jin is the spine of it; everything else here is optional, including the fight that decides whether the true ending is even open to you.

Story bosses, in order: Grief-Stricken Jin.

Optional in this chapter: One-Eyed Archer (独眼弓客), Yan Qiansui, the Zither Maiden (烟千岁), Heartpiercer (穿心者), Blizzard Blademaster (暴雪刀主), Acolyte Guhe (5 of the 6 encounters here are optional).

Do not leave without: Blizzard Blademaster at the Whiteshadow's Fall bell is the true-ending gate. If you leave the lake without clearing it, the ending branch closes and the walkthrough's last chapter changes shape.

Chapter 7: Mountain of Imprisonment

A straight climb with a hard right turn at the end. Iron Butcher, Bi Feng at the Commander's Platform, then Kui Yanyan hold the ascent; Yu Ding sits in the Mirage Estate training grounds and belongs to this stretch rather than the next chapter, despite the location name.

Story bosses, in order: Iron Butcher → Bi Feng, Giant Saber Commander (巨刀统领 白峰) → Kui Yanyan → Yu Ding, No. 12 Crescent Blade Puppet.

Optional in this chapter: Jade-Face (玉面郎君), Huangxing, the Kunlun Renegade (荒行子) (2 of the 6 encounters here are optional).

Do not leave without: Jade-Face is inside the Lady's Shrine temple ruins, and Huangxing, the Kunlun Renegade is at the very end of the region, past the point where most players turn back.

Chapter 8: Mirage Estate

The shortest chapter in the walkthrough: Lei Dang and Qiu Feng, back to back, with no travel between them worth mentioning. It exists to set up the climb.

Story bosses, in order: Lei Dang → Qiu Feng, the Crimson Boneblade (赤骨刀 邱风).

Optional in this chapter: Mo Yuan (莫渊) (1 of the 3 encounter here is optional).

Do not leave without: Mo Yuan is the only optional fight here, and the chapter is short enough that there is no reason to skip it.

Chapter 9: Mount Soulrend & endgame

The point of no return. Leng Tu and Herald of the Veil hold the ascent, Meng Hua sits at the peak and only exists on the true-ending branch, and Zuo Shang returns as The True Long for the final fight. The Last Battle triggers immediately after him, so there is no trip back to a bell once the climb starts.

Story bosses, in order: Leng Tu → Herald of the Veil → Meng Hua, Merciful Lady of the Blossom Veil (莫华) → Zuo Shang, The True Long → The Last Battle.

Optional in this chapter: The Saw and the Crusher (1 of the 6 encounter here is optional).

Do not leave without: The Saw and the Crusher is the only optional fight left in the endgame. Clear it before the final climb, not after, because after is not an option.

One structural note that applies to the whole walkthrough: bells are the fast-travel network, and they do not work inside the Phantom Illusionist Ruins. That is why the Four Guardians' Mirror realm reads as a one-way trip in the mission table - it is not a bug in the order, it is a region with the exit disabled until you clear it.

sections.title: Region Notes, In the Order You Hit Them
sections.content:
Weeping Creek Valley. Tutorial-by-stealth: the region exists to teach Sha-Chi. Peng Meng is the first real boss and drops the Dread Axe, your first Phantom Edge. Hua, Deadly Betrothed is optional and sits in the Flesh Lily Fields - fight her here, not later, because her drop (Scarlet Wraithblade) is one of the best early weapons and the fight is scaled for this point.

Crimson Forest. Two story bosses that teach the elemental vocabulary: Hua Qianxiao's drinking shield, Jing Ye's horse and blood-draining sword. Bai Chilian closes the region. Everything missable in the Village of Lu window should be resolved before the mirror puzzle.

Village of Lu. The densest optional region. Mu Xiaokui's encounter hands out more than one weapon, Yuzan drops the Heartrend Pipa, and four Tales start here. Clear it properly.

Pangzhen. The largest region and the widest missable window. Flame, the Lion Dance Grandmaster closes it and drops the Flaming Mane, which you need later to open the way into Pangzhen Slums for Acolyte Lei Ting. Do not leave before the Tales are done.

Mandate Encampment. Short. The Seven-Stars Formation is the fight that matters; clear the disciples before the leader or the leader has support.

Meigu Lake. Three separate systems converge here - the boat, the mirror realm, and the Blizzard Blademaster. This is where the true-ending checklist either comes together or falls apart.

Mountain of Imprisonment. Optional for the story, required for the true ending. The Yin Crystal Puppet Eye is here, and so are Bi Feng and Jade-Face.

Mount Soulrend. The endgame. Herald of the Veil, Bloodline Awakening's fifth pillar, Meng Hua, Zuo Shang, and then the hidden fight.

sections.title: The Point of No Return
sections.content:
The climb from the Mirage Estate to the peak of Mount Soulrend is the cutoff. The game warns you; the warning is not specific about what you are about to lose. Per 177xz, the warning appears even when every prerequisite is already met, so it is not a diagnostic - do not read it as one.

What expires: any purple Tale still open, the Acolyte scarecrow fights you have not triggered, the Crimson Manor secret boss, and the optional bosses in regions you have already passed.

What survives: free roam after the credits, bells, accessories and collectible cleanup, Tempering, and New Game Plus. So a missed item is recoverable; a missed Tale usually is not, because the trigger depends on a story state you cannot go back to.

sections.title: Before You Commit
sections.content:
• Manual save, separate slot, at the Mirage Estate.
  • Purple Tales: all done, none open.
  • Acolytes: four masks in hand.
  • Pillars: four destroyed plus the one in the mirror realm.
  • Crystal Puppet Eyes: two, from the Mountain of Imprisonment and the Crimson Manor.
  • Illusory Pipa: restored. Puppet's Tongue: used.
  • Quick Hand Zhang: all five relics delivered.

Anything not ticked, tick it now - the true ending checklist has the long version. For how much time the run should take, see how long to beat.

sections.title: Sources
sections.content:
Mission names and order: Gamer.org's chapter-and-mission list and TigerJek's chapter list, which agree on the sequence and differ on two region labels. Region structure and the semi-open framing: both, plus 18183's Chinese version. Point-of-no-return behaviour and the warning prompt: 177xz and VGTimes.

Not asserted here: an exact per-mission hour count. No source breaks the campaign down that finely, and the 20-25 hour figure is for the story as a whole.
